title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' notes, this page computes the conjectural motivic Galois group G of the Tannakian category of (numerical, pure) motives over the prime field F_p. It works modulo the standard conjectures and the Tate conjecture, which make the category semisimple and determine it by Frobenius eigenvalues.

(1) Weil numbers. Let Γ ⊂ Q̄* consist of the λ that satisfy three conditions:
- λ is an algebraic integer;
- λ is an ℓ-adic unit for every ℓ ≠ p;
- every conjugate λ_i has |λ_i| = p^{ν/2} for a suitable ν ∈ Z_{≥0}.
These are Weil p-numbers of weight ν. A q-Weil number with q = p^n is a p-Weil number of weight nν, so Γ already contains the Frobenius eigenvalues of all motives over all finite extensions F_{p^n}.

(2) The identity component. The identity component G^0 is the pro-torus whose character group is X*(G^0) = Γ/Γ_tors = Γ/μ_∞. Passing to F_{p^n} replaces λ by λ^n, so only Γ modulo roots of unity is intrinsic. G^0 is commutative and plays the role of the geometric motivic group over F̄_p. G/G^0 is then the profinite Galois group Ẑ of F_p. In modern terms G^0 is the Weil-number pro-torus P of Langlands–Rapoport and Milne.

(3) The Tate character. The Tate (Lefschetz) character ε: G → G_m corresponds on characters to Z → Γ, 1 ↦ p, because the Lefschetz motive has Frobenius eigenvalue p.

(4) The kernel H. Let H = Ker(ε|G^0). Its character group is Γ' = Γ/⟨μ_∞, p^ν⟩. To find the torsion of Γ', suppose λ^n = ζ·p^m. Then λ = ζ'·p^{m/n} with p^{m/n} > 0 real. The Weil condition forces m/n ∈ ½Z. So tors(Γ') ≅ Z/2, generated by the class of p^{1/2}, giving 0 → Z/2 → Γ' → Γ'/tors → 0. Dually this is 0 → H^0 → H → μ_2 → 0.

(5) Compactness. H^0 is a 'tore compact', i.e. anisotropic over R. Complex conjugation sends λ to p^ν/λ, which is ≡ λ^{-1} mod p^ν, so it acts as −1 on Γ'/tors. This is the finite-field shadow of the link between polarizations (Hodge standard conjecture) and compact real forms of the kernel of the weight.

(6) Splitting. The weight cocharacter i: G_m → G satisfies ε∘i = t^{±2}, so i(μ_2) ⊂ H. Its pairing with the class of p^{1/2} (weight 1) is nontrivial, so i|μ_2 maps isomorphically onto the quotient μ_2. Hence H ≅ H^0 × μ_2.

Purpose: to make explicit the structure of the motivic Galois group over a finite field and of its 'Mumford–Tate-type' kernel of the Tate character.
errors: As written, Γ is not a group: algebraic integers are not closed under inverses. One should take the group generated by such λ, or drop integrality and allow ν ∈ Z. Only Γ/torsion matters, so this is harmless.
'p^ν' in the quotient Γ/{racines de l'unité, p^ν} must mean the integer powers of p (ν ∈ Z). Otherwise p^{1/2} would be killed and the Z/2 would disappear.

If the end of the page really reads i|μ_2 : μ_2 → H^0 (it may), that is a slip. i(−1) is not in H^0, since it maps nontrivially to the μ_2 quotient; it lies in H, which is exactly why it splits the sequence.
The whole computation is conditional on the standard conjectures and the Tate conjecture (semisimplicity, and motives over F_q determined by Frobenius). This is implicit, not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Character group of the identity component of the motivic Galois group over F_p (equivalently the motivic group over F̄_p) is the group of Weil p-numbers modulo roots of unity.
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number pro-torus P (motivic group of motives over finite fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987); Milne, 'Motives over finite fields' (1994); framework in Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne–Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Only general mentions of the motivic Galois group in Récoltes et Semailles; no explicit Weil-number computation in his published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Tate character ε: G → G_m dual to 1 ↦ p.
ideas.modern_name: Tate/weight character of the motivic Galois group

ideas.what: Kernel H of ε on G^0 has character group Γ/⟨μ_∞, p^Z⟩, with torsion Z/2 generated by p^{1/2}; hence 0 → H^0 → H → μ_2 → 0.
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the kernel of the Tate character on the Weil-number torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Milne (1994) and the Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid

ideas.what: H^0 is a compact (R-anisotropic) torus, because complex conjugation acts as −1 on characters modulo p^ν.
ideas.modern_name: Compactness of the kernel of the weight as the polarization/positivity criterion (Deligne–Saavedra theory of polarized Tannakian categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (Hodge theory: Mumford–Tate group modulo weight is compact for CM/abelian types)

ideas.what: The weight cocharacter restricted to μ_2 splits H ≅ H^0 × μ_2.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting by the weight homomorphism w restricted to μ_2

missed.claim: An explicit 1965-era (possibly up to c.1977) computation by Grothendieck of the conjectural motivic Galois group over F_p as the Weil-number pro-torus, with the Tate character, the μ_2 component coming from p^{1/2}, compactness of H^0, and the splitting by the weight cocharacter. In the literature this description is usually attributed to Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Milne (1994).
missed.quote: le sous-groupe Γ ⊂ Q̄* formé des λ ... |λ_i| = p^{ν/2} ... Le groupe G^0 est défini par Γ/Γ_tors ... H^0 est un tore compact ... splitting H ≃ H^0 × μ_2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority and history point. It shows Grothendieck himself had the Weil-number torus description and its real-compactness/polarization feature, not just the general idea of a motivic Galois group. That is relevant to the history of the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture and of Tannakian motives.

missed.claim: The page explicitly ties compactness of the kernel of the Tate character (a positivity/polarization phenomenon) to the arithmetic of Weil numbers (complex conjugation sends λ to p^ν/λ). This anticipates the Saavedra–Deligne criterion that polarizations correspond to compact forms.
missed.quote: et H^0 est un tore compact
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows the link between the Hodge-type standard conjecture and the Riemann hypothesis for Weil numbers was already formulated group-theoretically by Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (Milne 1994, Langlands–Rapoport). It is notable as an early, explicit, unpublished computation by Grothendieck of the motivic Galois group over F_p in terms of Weil numbers, including the μ_2 component and compactness. The idea that he envisaged this is folklore, but this level of detail is not in his published record. Priority is moderately interesting rather than surprising.
